title: Rainwater on a Height Grid
src: Media.net OA, IIT Patna. Coding question 1 of 3 (the same problem as LeetCode 407). Also reported in a second Media.net set ("Rainwater Harvesting", N, M ≤ 110, heights ≥ 1).
body:
A rectangular island is described by an m × n grid heightMap, where each cell is a 1 × 1 column of the given height. After heavy rain, water collects on top of the cells wherever it can't run off. Water flows from a cell to its four side neighbours and leaves the island across the outer border.

Return the total volume of water that stays on the island.

Function to complete

Complete trapRainWater(heightMap). It returns the volume of trapped water.

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: First line: m and n. Then m lines of n integers each.

wrong.why: 1-D trapping on each row separately (ignores water escaping up or down)
level = min of the tallest cell in the four straight directions (water can leak around corners)

samples.ex: In the middle row, the cells of height 2 and 1 next to each other fill up to level 3 (1 + 2 units), and the 2 near the right end fills to 3 as well (1 unit): 4 in total.
The wall of 3s holds the water at level 3: eight cells of height 2 hold 1 each and the centre holds 2, so 10.
